statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures closed for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are not scheduled to reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, so no tradable Nasdaq-100 price path exists in any of the twenty-four hours published here, which expire about two hours before that reopen. Stress is 40, moderate: a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods is in force with talks suspended and a dollar-for-dollar Canadian match now dated to 8 September across steel, dairy, agricultural equipment and appliances, the latest H.15 column shows 4.19% at two years, 4.69% at ten and 5.23% at thirty with the long end at its highest since 2007, crude has gained more than 5% for a second consecutive week with the Strait of Hormuz constraint unresolved, and next week carries PCE, the second GDP estimate, Nvidia's results and a Jackson Hole keynote. Confidence is 87, high, because every index, volatility, yield, energy, venue, tariff and calendar input was re-verified against primary sources this hour, with one widely used quote page again returning a Nasdaq-100 level inconsistent with its own ETF and composite prints and resolved against two independent sources.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered the entire decline to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, below its own open and up 0.33% on the day, while QQQ closed 0.35% higher at 713.44 and VIX settled at 14.89 near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier carries over from observed structure. Friday internals were split rather than aligned, with software sectors firm, semiconductors 0.31% lower and megacaps five to three higher on dispersion of about 1.82%. Because the venue is shut, no hour in this horizon can generate the shallow-pullback or extreme-holding behaviour that would move Tail toward the block threshold, so Tail stays at its closed-venue floor while Stress carries the unpriced policy, rates and energy stack. The danger window is empty by construction: there is no tradable interval inside the published horizon.
headline: Closed-venue assessment: CME equity index futures stay halted across all twenty-four published hours, Canada's dollar-for-dollar answer to the 50% US tariff is dated to 8 September, and Tail holds the closed-venue floor of 4 with the horizon expiring about two hours before the Sunday reopen.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z, so the venue is confirmed shut across all twenty-four slots published here, which run from 2026-08-22T20:00:00Z to 2026-08-23T19:00:00Z and expire roughly two hours before that reopen. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 95.69 points or 0.33% from a 29,213.17 previous close, after opening at 29,359.60 and printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session and the close finished below the open, which is the shape of a market that still mean-reverts. One widely used quote page again returned an inconsistent Nasdaq-100 level this hour, and the 29,308.86 close was reconfirmed against an independent index quote and against QQQ at 713.44, up 0.35%, alongside a Nasdaq Composite close of 26,180.45, up 0.43%. VIX closed at 14.89, down 6.00%, near the bottom of a 14.77-15.95 range rather than at a stressed extreme. Trade policy is the first unpriced item: talks between Washington and Ottawa collapsed shortly before the Friday deadline, a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods took effect, and Prime Minister Carney suspended negotiations and confirmed a matching Canadian response from 8 September covering steel, dairy products, agricultural equipment and electrical appliances; the covered value is reported between roughly US$20bn and US$28bn depending on the outlet, so the exact figure is treated as uncertain here. The rates backdrop is the second unpriced item: the latest H.15 column for 20 August shows 4.19% at two years, 4.39% at five, 4.69% at ten and 5.23% at thirty against a 3.63% federal funds effective rate, with the long end at its highest since 2007 after a 5.34% print earlier in the week, and with the Treasury doubling long-bond buybacks to at least $4bn per operation from 9 September after the initial yield relief was fully unwound before the week ended. Energy is the third: WTI was last quoted near $87.06 and Brent near $94.39, a second consecutive weekly gain of more than 5%, with Strait of Hormuz traffic still muted, Iran-Oman shipping talks unconcluded and Tehran tying any reopening to sanctions relief; no fresh escalation has been reported across this weekend. Next week carries a dense checkpoint stack outside this horizon: consumer confidence, new home sales and a 2-year auction on 25 August, PCE and the second GDP estimate on 26 August alongside Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 results after the close, jobless claims and a 7-year auction on 27 August, and a Jackson Hole keynote from the current Fed Chair on 28 August. None of that can be expressed as a Nasdaq-100 price path before this forecast expires, which is why the whole stack sits in Stress and the forward calendar while Tail holds its closed-venue floor and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is close to complete: 22 hourly assessments are available, while the 05:00Z and 06:00Z clock-hours on 22 August have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across the available hours Tail held a narrow 4-10 band and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON throughout, so no hour approached the block threshold. The oldest slot still carries the tail end of the live Friday session at Tail 10 and Stress 48; after the futures halt at 21:00Z the dominant mode settled to normal and Tail fell to the closed-venue floor of 4, where it has stayed for the last 21 available hours. Stress fell to a 35-38 overnight band, rebuilt to 42 through the middle of Saturday as the tariff step took effect, and eased to 40-41 in the six most recent hours once the Canadian response was dated to 8 September. Confidence stayed in an 84-88 band throughout.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. All twenty-three remaining slots describe the same closed market: the final slot begins at 2026-08-23T19:00:00Z and ends about two hours before the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no live evidence can arrive before this forecast expires. Tail therefore holds 4 in every hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON, with the danger window empty because no tradable interval exists inside the horizon. Stress eases from 40 to a trough of 37 through the quiet Saturday night and Sunday overnight hours, then rebuilds steadily to 45 by the final slot as the reopen approaches with the tariff step, a post-2007 long end, a second consecutive weekly crude gain above 5%, the unresolved Hormuz constraint and next week's PCE, GDP, Nvidia and Jackson Hole checkpoints all still unpriced and facing a single opening auction. Confidence decays from 87 to 81 across the horizon purely because the last live price observation ages, not because any source degraded.
